name: Greater Romania
summary: Greater Romania is the Romanian nationalist ideal of uniting all Romanians in one state, first realised in 1918 with Transylvania, Bessarabia and Bukovina and lost in part in 1940. Today it survives as irredentism toward Moldova and parts of Ukraine, most visibly in the Greater Romania Party. Adherents combine ethnic nationalism, Orthodox-tinged social conservatism, and a state-centred, populist approach to the economy.
scope: The interwar Greater Romania ideal (the 1918 unions and the Kingdom of Romania within its 1919-1940 borders) together with its modern irredentist expression in the Greater Romania Party under Corneliu Vadim Tudor. The core positions are territorial and national; economic, social and procedural answers are mostly inferred from the party and the wider Romanian nationalist tradition. Excludes the Iron Guard's fascist programme as a separate strand.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a defining issue, but the Greater Romania Party's social-democratic, state-interventionist economics point toward public health provision.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The party proposes state intervention in the economy, so a committed adherent would doubt that unregulated markets beat government.

unions-good.rationale: Neither source documents a position; national-communist nostalgia and nationalist suspicion of class politics pull in opposite ways.

cut-welfare.rationale: A fiscally centre-left, populist party would not endorse welfare cuts.

strong-leader.rationale: The interwar monarchy drifted into royal dictatorship and the modern party centred on a charismatic leader, Tudor, who was praised alongside Antonescu.

state-harmful.rationale: The Greater Romania ideal is a state-building project; the state is the vehicle of national unity.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented stance; order-oriented nationalists generally accept firm state control of weapons.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: The party campaigned for tougher law enforcement, including capital punishment, and treats the army as a guardian of the nation.

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

decide-locally.rationale: The ideal is a unitary national state; the 1923 and 1938 constitutions centralised, and nationalists reject ethnic autonomy for regions.

traditional-family.rationale: Described as socially far-right and tied to Orthodox nationalism, which treats the family as the nation's base.

more-religion-public.rationale: Romanian nationalism ties Romanianness to Orthodoxy, and the Iron Guard's strong religious nationalism is part of the lineage.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending and uniting the Romanian nation and its culture is the ideology's reason for existing.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Ethno-nationalists favour limiting immigration, though it is not a prominent theme in the sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The party is softly Eurosceptic and sovereignty-minded, though it backed EU and NATO entry.

nation-first.rationale: National interest and unity of Romanians come before global cooperation in the party's sovereignty-focused politics.

open-borders.rationale: The ideal concerns redrawing borders to include Romanians, and ethno-nationalism rejects open borders.

revolution-justified.rationale: Adherents hold the 1918 union as legitimate nation-making but are largely order-minded; no clear stance on revolution.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Interwar Romanian industrialisation was protectionist and the party favours state economic intervention.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Interwar industrial policy emphasised heavy and arms industry, and the party's platform favours state intervention.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Alien to a nationalist, property-recognising programme.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Carol II's 1938 regime had corporatist features but it is not part of the core ideal.

one-party-rule.rationale: Carol II dissolved parties, yet the ideal itself is territorial and the party competes in elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.

reviewHistory.rationale: The Greater Romania state was the Kingdom of Romania and its unification under the crown is celebrated, though the modern party is not monarchist.

democracy-best.rationale: Interwar Greater Romania ended in royal dictatorship while the modern party contests elections; adherents are split.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mainstream adherents reject violence while the Iron Guard strand embraced it; genuinely split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Fascist-era nationalism glorified war but mainstream adherents do not state this.

separate-church-state.rationale: Orthodoxy is bound up with Romanian identity and the nationalist tradition favours church-nation links.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wikipedia describes the ideal as uniting people defined as Romanians in one state, with the aim of a homogeneous nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism puts the nation, not class, at the centre of history.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Romanian unification rests on shared language and ethnicity, not religion or civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nationalist ethics favour duty to nation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy does not appear in the documented positions of this ideology.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalist demographic concern favours population growth.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement looks to restoring the interwar Greater Romania and the national order lost in 1940.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Principled nationalist programme rather than pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Adherents work via elections and statecraft.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolishing the division of labour is a Marxist-utopian idea that has no place in an industrialising nationalist programme.

collective-farming.rationale: Interwar land reform created smallholders; Ceausescu-era collectivisation is a different strand.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory, rejected by nationalist adherents.

harm-principle.rationale: Social conservatives favour restricting conduct for morals and nation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The ideal prioritises the national collective; and nationalists contested minority group claims.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Libertarian view, alien to the ideology.

state-as-business.rationale: Statist nationalism sees citizens as members of a nation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Populist suspicion of elites, but no stated view.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The ideal was framed in biological and racial terms in the interwar period, but modern adherents rarely state this.

organic-representation.rationale: Carol II's regime had corporatist features but this is not core.

total-state.rationale: Authoritarian, but the ideal itself does not ask the state to direct culture and life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalists speak of reviving national greatness, yet decadence rhetoric is not prominent in the sources.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The core demand is annexing Moldova, Northern Bukovina and Bessarabia.

bound-labor.rationale: The 1918 resolution demanded radical land reform, the opposite.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Mixed, with Tudor styling himself philo-Semitic after 2003 while earlier antisemitism persisted.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The ideal is uniting Romanians abroad with the homeland; citizenship for Romanians in Moldova and beyond is a natural corollary.

revive-national-language.rationale: Romanian was never lost, though language unity is central to the movement.

national-self-determination.rationale: Greater Romania rests on Romanians' self-determination at Alba Iulia and Chernivtsi in 1918.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism holds that the nation transcends class, so partnership is the natural stance.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nationalism treats inherited cultural institutions as the substance of the nation, so adherents would refuse to sacrifice them.

workers-nation.rationale: National-communist heritage and nationalism prefer a national framework over the Marxist International.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest prohibition has no place in Romanian nationalist or Orthodox tradition and is not in any documented programme.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Interwar Romania used ethnic discrimination, but the ideology does not demand racial segregation by law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This Marxist account of the state conflicts with the nationalist view of the state as embodying the whole nation.

national-mission.rationale: The ideal is about Romania's own unification, not spreading its system.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-corruption populism is central to the party's rhetoric.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Interwar racial biopolitics existed but no stated stance.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The party rejected the 2006 report on communist crimes as manipulation and praised the Ceausescu regime.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The party's state-intervention platform and the interwar state-led industrial drive contradict a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial tropes appeared in the ideal, but no documented stance on this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Adherents are split, from Alba Iulia egalitarian rhetoric to ethnic hierarchy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: National communism asserted socialism in one nation.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A unitary nation-state favours uniform law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Orthodox nationalists dislike proselytising but no documented stance.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Orthodox religious instruction is part of Romanian nationalism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents invoke popular assembly consent in 1918 yet royal and party authoritarian practice varied.

population-transfer.rationale: Antonescu era saw deportations but no stated mainstream position.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A pacifist-libertarian rule is incompatible with an ideology demanding annexation and capital punishment.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fascist-era social Darwinism existed but not as mainstream.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The party called for outlawing UDMR as a separatist party.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist vanguardism is not part of nationalist doctrine, though the party's Ceausescu nostalgia leaves it unclear.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The sources record no stance on prioritising the poor, and populist and nationalist concerns pull in different directions.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Interwar governments repressed strikes violently; order-oriented.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The nationalist case for a homogeneous state holds multiethnic composition produced conflict.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is alien to the party-based electoral politics adherents contest.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Carol II suspended civil liberties in 1938 and the party praised Antonescu and Ceausescu, regimes that used emergency powers against internal enemies.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Ethnic nationalists favour restrictive naturalisation for outsiders while descent-based citizenship remains open.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Carol II's constitution strengthened royal power.

clerical-rule.rationale: The ideology is nationalist rather than clerical; the church is an ally but not the ruler.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The party kept NATO presence and backed EU entry.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reuniting Romanians divided from Romania by Soviet and post-Soviet borders, especially Moldova, is the central aim.

death-penalty.rationale: Restoring capital punishment was a plank of Tudor's 2000 campaign for the Greater Romania Party, but it is not a position of the Greater Romania ideal itself.

minority-language-support.rationale: 1918 resolution promised national freedom but nationalists disputed autonomy and the 1923 constitution neglected minorities.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1918 resolution invoked a universally elected constituent assembly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: A nation-first outlook would give priority to domestic needs over global aid duties.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Tudor ran for president, but no stated view.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Adherents claim Bessarabia, Bukovina as historic Romanian land and refuse to cede.

collective-defense.rationale: The party kept Romania's NATO membership, which rests on mutual defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Soviet annexation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina in 1940 is held unlawful.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Greater Romania was a monarchy, with the crown as national symbol, though Carol II was partisan in practice.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Carol II's royal dictatorship, but not core.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Greater Romania demands uniting Romanian-populated lands in neighbouring states, the ideal summed up as from the Dniester to the Tisza.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The ideal is to unite all Romanians, including Moldova's, across existing borders in one state.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The 1918 Alba Iulia resolution promised minorities their own schools and administration, but the nationalist ideal is a unitary Romanian nation-state and the party opposed Hungarian autonomy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Interwar Greater Romania was a monarchy while the modern party is republican-leaning, so adherents split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Romanian nationalism treats national history, language and Orthodox heritage as the core of schooling and identity.

patriotic-education.rationale: Ethnic and religious nationalism holds that schools should instil national pride and loyalty, as the Greater Romania Party platform stresses.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Romania had no empire of its own; the ideal is union of Romanians, not influence over a former imperial realm.

delink-world-market.rationale: The party is protectionist and sceptical of the EU and free trade, but delinking from the world market is not proposed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1918 Alba Iulia resolution promised civil and minority freedoms, but the modern party prefers duties and national interest; adherents are split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Alba Iulia Resolution rested on an assembly of the nation as the source of legitimacy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Reunifying Romanian-inhabited lands lost in 1940 and held by Moldova and Ukraine is the defining demand.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The party's economic nationalism opposes sale of national assets to foreign buyers.

single-official-language.rationale: The party and Romanian nationalism treat Romanian as the sole state language and oppose autonomy for Hungarian-speaking regions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The party's economic nationalism includes keeping land and national assets in Romanian hands.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Tudor and the party have promoted claims of hostile minorities, notably Hungarians and Roma, acting against Romania, as documented in the party and Tudor articles.

informal-organisation.rationale: The ideal of a unified Romanian state is pursued through formal state and party institutions, and informal anarchist-style organizing is foreign to it.

religious-nation.rationale: Romanian nationalism is closely linked to Orthodoxy, which the sources describe as part of national identity, though the core definition remains ethnic.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The ideal is a unitary nation-state, not self-governing communes.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Greater Romania rests on the claim to unite all historically Romanian lands, including Moldova and Bukovina, in one state.

social-market-economy.rationale: The party's state-centred, nominally centre-left economics rejects laissez-faire but also favours state intervention beyond a social market; split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The nationalism is built on defending and extending the national state, including by force of arms, so it cannot imagine abolishing the army.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Interwar Greater Romania was a monarchy, but the modern Greater Romania Party is republican in outlook; adherents are split.

term-limits.rationale: Not an issue the party or the interwar ideal addressed; populist anti-elite sentiment pulls toward limits while a strong-leader tradition pulls against.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Romanian nationalism holds that Romanians descend continuously from the Dacians and Romans, and the party and the wider tradition insist on this lineage.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Romanian nationalism honours fallen soldiers and heroes of the 1918 unification and Orthodox-tinged nationalism treats them as martyrs and saints.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Orthodox-tinged Romanian nationalism frames the nation's struggle in religious terms, though the sources give no explicit statement.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The ideal is to gather all Romanians within one state, so a homeland serving as a cultural centre in place of gathering is rejected.

culture-before-state.rationale: Greater Romania placed political union first (1918) and treats the state as the vehicle of the nation, over cultural renewal as a prior step.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The party and interwar Romanian nationalism favoured Romanianisation of the economy and ethnic homogeneity, and the sources record this aim.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Romanian nationalism is ethnic, treating the Romanian nation as the political unit; read as ethnic rather than racial, at low confidence.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The ideal is irredentist, seeking to unite Romanians across borders, which cannot be limited to defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The ideal unites Romanians, notably the Romanian-speaking population of Moldova, across state borders, and the Alba Iulia resolution grounded union in the shared Romanian nation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Greater Romania Party accuses Hungary and other neighbours of working to detach Transylvania, and the interwar state lost territory in 1940.

sacred-nation.rationale: Romanian nationalism treats the nation as an enduring ethnic and Orthodox-tinged community whose unity across generations is the goal.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Greater Romania holds that Moldovan is simply Romanian and that Romanians in Moldova and Ukraine belong to one nation, so a language under several regional names is one language.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1918 Alba Iulia resolution called for universal suffrage, and nothing in the later movement contests it.

national-church-status.rationale: Romanian nationalism closely links the nation with the Orthodox Church, which the party defends as the national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Greater Romania Party opposes autonomy for Hungarian-majority areas and the unitary national state is central to the ideal.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Adherents cite the 1918 Alba Iulia assembly as popular will for union, but reject local votes for Hungarian-majority areas; split.

simple-living.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to simple living; economic outlook is state-centred, with no austerity ideal.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Romanian nationalism ties the nation to ancestral land, and the Greater Romania ideal is the duty to hold and reunite the lands of the Dniester-to-Tisza homeland.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The ideal is uniting Romanians outside the state, and the party claims Moldova and Bukovina on behalf of ethnic Romanians there.

national-resource-control.rationale: The party's state-centred, nationalist economics favours national rather than foreign control of resources.

police-more-powers.rationale: The party campaigned for tougher law enforcement, including capital punishment, and treats the army as a guardian of the nation. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: A fiscally centre-left, populist party would not endorse welfare cuts. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A state may claim territory outside its borders because people of its nationality live there.
missingStatements.rationale: Greater Romania demands uniting Romanian-populated lands in neighbouring states, the ideal summed up as from the Dniester to the Tisza.

missingStatements.text: A political party representing an ethnic minority should be banned if it is suspected of working to separate a region from the country.
missingStatements.rationale: The Greater Romania Party called for outlawing the ethnic Hungarian party UDMR, accusing it of plotting Transylvanian secession.

notes: Interwar and modern strands differ: the interwar kingdom was a monarchy ending in royal dictatorship, while the modern party is populist, nominally centre-left on economics and nostalgic for Ceausescu. Most economic, social and procedural answers are inferred and low confidence, so inclusion may be thin.
